mediaType.description: The media type of the object, optionally including media type parameters. The media type can provide additional context about the kind of data being represented, such as an image, font, or executable.

attachment.title: Attachment
attachment.description: Specifies the metadata and content for an attachment.

encoding.title: Encoding
encoding.description: Specifies the optional encoding the text is represented in.

meta:enum.base64: Base64 is a binary-to-text encoding scheme that represents binary data in an ASCII string.

content.title: Attachment Text
content.description: The attachment data. Proactive controls such as input validation and sanitization should be employed to prevent misuse of attachment text.

externalReferences.title: External References
externalReferences.description: External references provide a way to document systems, sites, and information that may be relevant but are not included with the BOM. They may also establish specific relationships within or external to the BOM.

externalReference.title: External Reference
externalReference.description: External references provide a way to document systems, sites, and information that may be relevant but are not included with the BOM. They may also establish specific relationships within or external to the BOM.

url.title: URL
url.description: The URI (URL or URN) to the external reference. External references are URIs and therefore can accept any URL scheme including https ([RFC-7230](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc7230.txt)), mailto ([RFC-2368](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc2368.txt)), tel ([RFC-3966](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc3966.txt)), and dns ([RFC-4501](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc4501.txt)). External references may also include formally registered URNs such as [CycloneDX BOM-Link](https://cyclonedx.org/capabilities/bomlink/) to reference CycloneDX BOMs or any object within a BOM. BOM-Link transforms applicable external references into relationships that can be expressed in a BOM or across BOMs.

comment.title: Comment
comment.description: A comment describing the external reference

type.title: Type
type.description: Specifies the type of external reference.

meta:enum.issue-tracker: Issue or defect tracking system, or an Application Lifecycle Management (ALM) system
meta:enum.bom: Bill of Materials (SBOM, OBOM, HBOM, SaaSBOM, etc)
meta:enum.source-distribution: The location where the source code distributable can be obtained. This is often an archive format such as zip or tgz. The source-distribution type complements use of the version control (vcs) type.
meta:enum.distribution-intake: The location where a component was published to. This is often the same as "distribution" but may also include specialized publishing processes that act as an intermediary.
meta:enum.license: The reference to the license file. If a license URL has been defined in the license node, it should also be defined as an external reference for completeness.
meta:enum.build-meta: Build-system specific meta file (i.e. pom.xml, package.json, .nuspec, etc)
meta:enum.build-system: Reference to an automated build system
meta:enum.security-contact: Specifies a way to contact the maintainer, supplier, or provider in the event of a security incident. Common URIs include links to a disclosure procedure, a mailto (RFC-2368) that specifies an email address, a tel (RFC-3966) that specifies a phone number, or dns (RFC-4501) that specifies the records containing DNS Security TXT.
meta:enum.model-card: A model card describes the intended uses of a machine learning model, potential limitations, biases, ethical considerations, training parameters, datasets used to train the model, performance metrics, and other relevant data useful for ML transparency.
meta:enum.log: A record of events that occurred in a computer system or application, such as problems, errors, or information on current operations.
meta:enum.configuration: Parameters or settings that may be used by other components or services.
meta:enum.evidence: Information used to substantiate a claim.
meta:enum.formulation: Describes the formulation of any referencable object within the CycloneDX artifact or payload, including components, services, metadata, declarations, or the CycloneDX artifact or payload itself.
meta:enum.attestation: Human or machine-readable statements containing facts, evidence, or testimony.
meta:enum.threat-model: An enumeration of identified weaknesses, threats, and countermeasures, dataflow diagram (DFD), attack tree, and other supporting documentation in human-readable or machine-readable format.
meta:enum.adversary-model: The defined assumptions, goals, and capabilities of an adversary.
meta:enum.risk-assessment: Identifies and analyzes the potential of future events that may negatively impact individuals, assets, and/or the environment. Risk assessments may also include judgments on the tolerability of each risk.
meta:enum.hazard-analysis: A hazard analysis, such as a hazard analysis and risk assessment (HARA), a failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA), or a fault tree analysis (FTA).
meta:enum.safety-case: A structured argument, supported by a body of evidence, that a system is acceptably safe for a given application in a given environment.
meta:enum.vulnerability-assertion: A Vulnerability Disclosure Report (VDR) which asserts the known and previously unknown vulnerabilities that affect a component, service, or product including the analysis and findings describing the impact (or lack of impact) that the reported vulnerability has on a component, service, or product.
meta:enum.exploitability-statement: A Vulnerability Exploitability eXchange (VEX) which asserts the known vulnerabilities that do not affect a product, product family, or organization, and optionally the ones that do. The VEX should include the analysis and findings describing the impact (or lack of impact) that the reported vulnerability has on the product, product family, or organization.
meta:enum.pentest-report: Results from an authorized simulated cyberattack on a component or service, otherwise known as a penetration test.
meta:enum.static-analysis-report: SARIF or proprietary machine or human-readable report for which static analysis has identified code quality, security, and other potential issues with the source code.
meta:enum.dynamic-analysis-report: Dynamic analysis report that has identified issues such as vulnerabilities and misconfigurations.
meta:enum.runtime-analysis-report: Report generated by analyzing the call stack of a running application.
meta:enum.test-report: Results of testing, such as a laboratory test, a verification test, or a validation test, of a component, service, or system.
meta:enum.incident-report: A report of an incident, such as a safety incident, a security incident, or an operational failure, and its investigation.
meta:enum.component-analysis-report: Report generated by Software Composition Analysis (SCA), container analysis, or other forms of component analysis.
meta:enum.maturity-report: Report containing a formal assessment of an organization, business unit, or team against a maturity model.
meta:enum.certification-report: Industry, regulatory, or other certification from an accredited (if applicable) certification body.
meta:enum.codified-infrastructure: Code or configuration that defines and provisions virtualized infrastructure, commonly referred to as Infrastructure as Code (IaC).
meta:enum.quality-metrics: Report or system in which quality metrics can be obtained.
meta:enum.poam: Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&M) complement an "attestation" external reference. POA&M is defined by NIST as a "document that identifies tasks needing to be accomplished. It details resources required to accomplish the elements of the plan, any milestones in meeting the tasks and scheduled completion dates for the milestones".
meta:enum.perspective: A CycloneDX perspective defines a domain-specific view, enabling different audiences to interpret and navigate the data through their own conceptual lens.
meta:enum.electronic-signature: An e-signature is commonly a scanned representation of a written signature or a stylized script of the person's name.
meta:enum.digital-signature: A signature that leverages cryptography, typically public/private key pairs, which provides strong authenticity verification.
meta:enum.rfc-9116: Document that complies with [RFC 9116](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc9116.html) (A File Format to Aid in Security Vulnerability Disclosure)
meta:enum.patent: References information about patents which may be defined in human-readable documents or in machine-readable formats such as CycloneDX or ST.96. For detailed patent information or to reference the information provided directly by patent offices, it is recommended to leverage standards from the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) such as [ST.96](https://www.wipo.int/standards/en/st96).
meta:enum.patent-family: References information about a patent family which may be defined in human-readable documents or in machine-readable formats such as CycloneDX or ST.96. A patent family is a group of related patent applications or granted patents that cover the same or similar invention. For detailed patent family information or to reference the information provided directly by patent offices, it is recommended to leverage standards from the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) such as [ST.96](https://www.wipo.int/standards/en/st96).
meta:enum.patent-assertion: References assertions made regarding patents associated with a component or service. Assertions distinguish between ownership, licensing, and other relevant interactions with patents.
meta:enum.citation: A reference to external citations applicable to the object identified in a CycloneDX artifact or payload or the CycloneDX artifact or payload itself. When used with a BOM-Link, this allows offloading citations into a separate CycloneDX artifacts or payloads.
meta:enum.swid-tag: A Software Identification (SWID) tag document conforming to ISO/IEC 19770-2. The reference resolves to the XML SoftwareIdentity document itself, including all of its metadata (entities, evidence, payload, links, and meta elements). This is distinct from the `swid` identifier scheme, which carries only the tagId of a SWID tag.
meta:enum.gs1-digital-link: A [GS1 Digital Link URI](https://ref.gs1.org/standards/digital-link/uri-syntax/) that connects the component's GS1 identification key, such as a GTIN, to online sources of information, including product data, safety documentation, digital product passports, and recall status. The URI may include key qualifiers, such as a batch or serial number, enabling identification at the class, batch, or individual item level. Component identity shall be derived from the component's identifiers, not from keys embedded in this URI.
meta:enum.other: Use this if no other types accurately describe the purpose of the external reference.

hashes.title: Hashes
hashes.description: The hashes of the external reference (if applicable).

postalAddress.title: Postal address
postalAddress.description: An address used to identify a contactable location.

refId.title: Reference Identifier
refId.description:
An optional identifier which can be used to reference the address elsewhere in the document. Every `refId` shall be unique within the document.
Value should not start with the BOM-Link intro 'urn:cdx:' to avoid conflicts with BOM-Links.

country.title: Country
country.description: The country name or the two-letter ISO 3166-1 country code.

region.title: Region
region.description: The region or state in the country.

locality.title: Locality
locality.description: The locality or city within the country.

refId.title: Reference Identifier
refId.description:
An optional identifier which can be used to reference the object elsewhere in the document. Every `refId` shall be unique within the document.
Value should not start with the BOM-Link intro 'urn:cdx:' to avoid conflicts with BOM-Links.

name.title: Organization Name
name.description: The name of the organization

address.title: Organization Address
address.description: The physical address (location) of the organization

url.title: Organization URL(s)
url.description: The URL of the organization. Multiple URLs are allowed.

contact.title: Organizational Contact
contact.description: A contact at the organization. Multiple contacts are allowed.

origins.title: Organization Origins
origins.description: The geographic origins associated with the organization, such as the country or countries where its goods or services originate. Multiple origins are allowed, each calculated on a different basis.

refId.title: Reference Identifier
refId.description:
An optional identifier which can be used to reference the object elsewhere in the document. Every `refId` shall be unique within the document.
Value should not start with the BOM-Link intro 'urn:cdx:' to avoid conflicts with BOM-Links.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name of a contact

email.title: Email Address
email.description: The email address of the contact.

phone.title: Phone
phone.description: The phone number of the contact.

origin.title: Origin
origin.description: Describes the geographic origin of the subject (for example, a component or party), expressed as a distribution across one or more countries or subdivisions, calculated on a stated basis. An origin may be scoped to a lifecycle or transformation stage, enabling stage-specific provenance such as distinguishing where a material was mined from where it was melted.

stage.title: Origin Stage
stage.description: The lifecycle or transformation stage of the subject to which this origin applies. When omitted, the origin describes the subject as a whole.

oneOf.title: Predefined Origin Stage
oneOf.description: An origin stage drawn from the predefined set.

meta:enum.designed: Creation of the design, specifications, or intellectual property of the subject, such as product design or integrated circuit design.
meta:enum.mined: Extraction of raw material from the earth, including ore mining and quarrying.
meta:enum.harvested: Collection of biologically derived raw material, such as timber, fibres, or natural rubber.
meta:enum.recycled: Recovery of material from scrap, waste, or previously used items.
meta:enum.refined: Purification of material, including chemical refining and electrorefining.
meta:enum.separated: Separation of individual elements or compounds from a mixed feedstock, such as rare earth element separation.
meta:enum.smelted: Extraction of metal from ore or concentrate by smelting.
meta:enum.melted: Melting of material into a homogeneous mass, such as an alloying melt or a remelt.
meta:enum.processed: Intermediate transformation not covered by a more specific stage, such as milling, atomization, or heat treatment.
meta:enum.manufactured: Fabrication of the item from its input materials or parts.
meta:enum.assembled: Integration of constituent parts into the finished item.
meta:enum.developed: Authoring of the source code of software or firmware.
meta:enum.built: Production of software artifacts from source, including compilation, packaging, and container image assembly.
meta:enum.tested: Verification of the subject against its requirements, such as software testing, hardware qualification, or final device test.
meta:enum.collected: Gathering of data from its sources, such as measurements, records, or user generated content.
meta:enum.trained: Training of a machine learning model, attributed to the regions where the training computation was performed.
meta:enum.hosted: Provision of the infrastructure on which a service or data resides, such as data centre regions.
meta:enum.operated: Operation and administration of the subject, attributed to the regions where operating personnel or systems are located.
meta:enum.maintained: Ongoing maintenance of the subject after release, including updates, patches, and security fixes.

oneOf.title: Custom Origin Stage
oneOf.description: An origin stage that is not present in the predefined set.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name of the custom origin stage.

description.title: Description
description.description: Description of the custom origin stage.

basis.title: Origin Basis
basis.description: A free-form description of the methodology or unit on which the origin distribution is calculated. Each origin of the same subject shall use a distinct combination of stage and basis.

distribution.title: Origin Distribution
distribution.description: The distribution of the origin across regions. The percentages of all entries shall total 100, within rounding of the stated precision.

originRegion.title: Origin Region
originRegion.description: A single region of origin, its share of the whole, and optionally the party that performed the stage in that region.

isoCode.title: ISO Code
isoCode.description: The country or subdivision of origin, expressed as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (for example, 'CA' for Canada) or an ISO 3166-2 subdivision code (for example, 'US-CA' for California, United States).

value.title: Value
value.description: The amount of the whole attributable to this region, expressed on the basis of the origin, for example a number of parts, a net weight, or a manufacturing cost. The values of all entries in a distribution sum to the whole, and each percentage is the value divided by that sum.

percentage.title: Percentage
percentage.description: The percentage of the whole attributable to this region. The percentages of all entries in a distribution must total 100, within rounding of the stated precision.

performedBy.title: Performed By
performedBy.description: Reference to the party that performed this stage of origin for this share of the distribution, such as the smelter that melted a material or the organization that developed a software component. Entries in a distribution may repeat a region in order to attribute shares to different parties.

properties.title: Properties
properties.description: Provides the ability to document properties in a name-value store. This provides flexibility to include data not officially supported in the standard without having to use additional namespaces or create extensions. Unlike key-value stores, properties support duplicate names, each potentially having different values. Property names of interest to the general public are encouraged to be registered in the [CycloneDX Property Taxonomy](https://github.com/CycloneDX/cyclonedx-property-taxonomy). Formal registration is optional.

property.title: Lightweight name-value pair
property.description: Provides the ability to document properties in a name-value store. This provides flexibility to include data not officially supported in the standard without having to use additional namespaces or create extensions. Unlike key-value stores, properties support duplicate names, each potentially having different values. Property names of interest to the general public are encouraged to be registered in the [CycloneDX Property Taxonomy](https://github.com/CycloneDX/cyclonedx-property-taxonomy). Formal registration is optional.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name of the property. Duplicate names are allowed, each potentially having a different value.

extensibleProperties.title: Extensible Properties
extensibleProperties.$comment: This is a mixin. It intentionally does NOT restrict additional/unevaluated properties itself; schemas composing it via `allOf` are expected to close themselves with `unevaluatedProperties: false` so that both their own defined properties and these patternProperties remain usable.

^ext:[a-zA-Z0-9.-]+\\.[a-zA-Z]{2,}:.+$.description:
CycloneDX supports a structured and namespace-aware mechanism for extensibility through the use of extensible properties. This mechanism enables organizations, ecosystems, and tool vendors to safely introduce custom properties without conflicting with the core schema or other extensions.

Extensible properties are defined as a JSON object whose keys must conform to a strict pattern that resembles a reverse domain name structure, prefixed with ext:. This pattern provides a namespacing convention that aligns with well-established practices in other structured formats (e.g., XML namespaces).

Values that are objects must declare the schema they conform to via `$schema`. This requirement applies recursively to objects contained in arrays, at any nesting depth.

propertyObject.title: Extensible Property Object
propertyObject.$comment:
Internal helper for extensibleProperties. Not part of the public schema API — do not reference externally; may change without notice.

This is a mixin.

propertyValue.title: Extensible Property Value
propertyValue.$comment:
Internal helper for extensibleProperties. Not part of the public schema API — do not reference externally; may change without notice.
Recursive: objects must declare a `$schema`, arrays may nest arbitrarily deep with the same rule applied to every item, all other values are plain scalars.

ordinalVersion.title: Ordinal Version
ordinalVersion.description: An ordinal version is a dot-delimited, purely numeric identifier where each segment represents an ordered level in the hierarchy. The segments have no prescribed meaning beyond numeric ordering, allowing straightforward comparison and sorting.

lifecycle.title: Lifecycle
lifecycle.description: The product lifecycle(s) that this BOM represents.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name of the lifecycle phase

description.title: Description
description.description: The description of the lifecycle phase

lifecycles.title: Lifecycles
lifecycles.description: Lifecycles communicate the stage(s) in which data in the BOM was captured. Different types of data may be available at various phases of a lifecycle, such as the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC), IT Asset Management (ITAM), and Software Asset Management (SAM). Thus, a BOM may include data specific to or only obtainable in a given lifecycle.

phase.title: Phase
phase.description: A pre-defined phase in the product lifecycle.

meta:enum.design: BOM produced early in the development lifecycle containing an inventory of components and services that are proposed or planned to be used. The inventory may need to be procured, retrieved, or resourced prior to use.
meta:enum.pre-build: BOM consisting of information obtained prior to a build process and may contain source files and development artifacts and manifests. The inventory may need to be resolved and retrieved prior to use.
meta:enum.build: BOM consisting of information obtained during a build process where component inventory is available for use. The precise versions of resolved components are usually available at this time as well as the provenance of where the components were retrieved from.
meta:enum.post-build: BOM consisting of information obtained after a build process has completed and the resulting components(s) are available for further analysis. Built components may exist as the result of a CI/CD process, may have been installed or deployed to a system or device, and may need to be retrieved or extracted from the system or device.
meta:enum.operations: BOM produced that represents inventory that is running and operational. This may include staging or production environments and will generally encompass multiple SBOMs describing the applications and operating system, along with HBOMs describing the hardware that makes up the system. Operations Bill of Materials (OBOM) can provide full-stack inventory of runtime environments, configurations, and additional dependencies.
meta:enum.discovery: BOM consisting of information observed through network discovery providing point-in-time enumeration of embedded, on-premise, and cloud-native services such as server applications, connected devices, microservices, and serverless functions.
meta:enum.decommission: BOM containing inventory that will be, or has been retired from operations.

tags.title: Tags
tags.description: Textual strings that aid in discovery, search, and retrieval of the associated object. Tags often serve as a way to group or categorize similar or related objects by various attributes.

uid.title: UID
uid.description: A unique identifier of the commit. This may be version control specific. For example, Subversion uses revision numbers whereas git uses commit hashes.

url.title: URL
url.description: The URL to the commit. This URL will typically point to a commit in a version control system.

author.title: Author
author.description: The author who created the changes in the commit

committer.title: Committer
committer.description: The person who committed or pushed the commit

message.title: Message
message.description: The text description of the contents of the commit

refId.title: Reference Identifier
refId.description: An identifier which can be used to reference the patch elsewhere in the document, such as from an annotation. Every `refId` shall be unique within the document.

meta:enum.unofficial: A patch which is not developed by the creators or maintainers of the software being patched. Refer to [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unofficial_patch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unofficial_patch).
meta:enum.monkey: A patch which dynamically modifies runtime behavior. Refer to [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monkey_patch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monkey_patch).
meta:enum.backport: A patch which takes code from a newer version of the software and applies it to older versions of the same software. Refer to [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backporting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backporting).
meta:enum.cherry-pick: A patch created by selectively applying commits from other versions or branches of the same software.

type.title: Patch Type
type.description: Specifies the purpose for the patch including the resolution of defects, security issues, or new behavior or functionality.

diff.title: Diff
diff.description: The patch file (or diff) that shows changes. Refer to [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diff)

oneOf.title: Resolved Reference
oneOf.description: A reference to the item the patch resolves, such as a weakness, vulnerability, use case, requirement, or threat declared elsewhere.

ref.title: Reference
ref.description: Reference using bom-link or `refId` to the resolved item.

resolves.title: Resolves
resolves.description: A collection of items the patch resolves. Each entry is an inline issue or a reference to the weakness, vulnerability, use case, requirement, or threat that the patch resolves.

patchReference.title: Patch Reference
patchReference.description: A reference to a patch declared elsewhere, such as in the definitions registry, in another position of the same document, or in another document via BOM-Link. A reference includes the referenced patch exactly as declared: every position that references the same patch includes an identical patch. Where the context differs, declare the patch inline instead.

ref.title: Reference
ref.description: Reference using bom-link or `refId` to the patch.

diff.title: Diff
diff.description: The patch file (or diff) that shows changes. Refer to https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diff

text.title: Diff text
text.description: Specifies the optional text of the diff

url.title: URL
url.description: Specifies the URL to the diff

issue.title: Issue
issue.description: An individual issue that has been resolved.

meta:enum.defect: A fault, flaw, or bug in software.
meta:enum.enhancement: A new feature or behavior in software.
meta:enum.security: A special type of defect which impacts security.

type.title: Issue Type
type.description: Specifies the type of issue

id.title: Issue ID
id.description: The identifier of the issue assigned by the source of the issue

name.title: Issue Name
name.description: The name of the issue

description.title: Issue Description
description.description: A description of the issue

source.title: Source
source.description: The source of the issue where it is documented

name.title: Name
name.description: The name of the source.

url.title: URL
url.description: The url of the issue documentation as provided by the source

references.title: References
references.description: A collection of URL's for reference. Multiple URLs are allowed.

timestamp.title: Timestamp
timestamp.description: The timestamp in which the action occurred

name.title: Name
name.description: The name of the individual who performed the action

email.title: E-mail
email.description: The email address of the individual who performed the action

locale.title: Locale
locale.description: Defines a syntax for representing two character language code (ISO-639) followed by an optional two character country code. The language code must be lower case. If the country code is specified, the country code must be upper case. The language code and country code must be separated by a minus sign. Examples: en, en-US, fr, fr-CA

measure.title: Measure
measure.description: A quantity expressed as a numeric value and a unit. Contexts that use this definition may constrain the permitted units, as the energy and carbon dioxide equivalent measures do. Dimensionless quantities and counts use the unit one, written as 1.

value.title: Value
value.description: The numeric value of the quantity.

unit.title: Unit
unit.description: The unit of the quantity, given as a predefined unit symbol or as a custom unit.

unitSymbol.title: Unit Symbol
unitSymbol.description: A predefined unit symbol. The symbols cover time, data size, throughput, compute, energy, carbon dioxide equivalent, and ratio quantities. The unit one, written as 1, is used for counts and dimensionless quantities. Where a symbol differs from its UCUM code, the code is noted in its definition.

meta:enum.1: The unit one, used for counts and for dimensionless quantities such as scores, fractions, and ratings.
meta:enum.ns: Nanoseconds, commonly used for high precision timing measurements.
meta:enum.us: Microseconds, commonly used for fine grained latency measurements.
meta:enum.ms: Milliseconds, commonly used for latency measurements.
meta:enum.s: Seconds, commonly used for latency and duration measurements.
meta:enum.min: Minutes, commonly used for duration measurements.
meta:enum.h: Hours, commonly used for duration measurements.
meta:enum.requests/s: Requests per second, commonly used for API and service throughput measurements, UCUM {request}/s.
meta:enum.ops/s: Operations per second, commonly used for general throughput measurements, UCUM {operation}/s.
meta:enum.tokens/s: Tokens per second, commonly used for language model throughput measurements, UCUM {token}/s.
meta:enum.FLOP: Total floating point operations, commonly used to express cumulative training compute, UCUM {FLOP}.
meta:enum.FLOPS: Floating point operations per second, UCUM {FLOP}/s.
meta:enum.GFLOPS: Billion floating point operations per second, UCUM G{FLOP}/s.
meta:enum.TFLOPS: Trillion floating point operations per second, UCUM T{FLOP}/s.
meta:enum.PFLOPS: Quadrillion floating point operations per second, UCUM P{FLOP}/s.
meta:enum.kWh: Kilowatt hour, the energy delivered by one kilowatt of power for one hour, UCUM kW.h.
meta:enum.tCO2eq: Tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, UCUM t{CO2eq}.
meta:enum.%: Percentage, commonly used for accuracy, precision, recall, availability, and other ratio based metrics.
meta:enum.ppm: Parts per million, a dimensionless unit expressing the ratio of one part per million parts, UCUM [ppm].

customUnit.title: Custom Unit
customUnit.description: A unit that the predefined unit symbols do not cover. Use a predefined unit symbol where one exists. A custom unit should be identified by its code in an established unit system, such as UCUM, UN/ECE Recommendation 20, or QUDT, so that consumers can validate and convert it.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name or symbol of the custom unit.

description.title: Description
description.description: A description of the custom unit.

system.title: Unit System
system.description: The unit system or code list in which the code is defined.

meta:enum.ucum: The [Unified Code for Units of Measure](https://ucum.org/), whose codes are case-sensitive strings such as kg, By, or {token}/s.
meta:enum.unece-rec20: [UN/ECE Recommendation 20](https://unece.org/trade/uncefact/cl-recommendations), whose codes are two or three character strings such as KWH or C26.
meta:enum.qudt: The [QUDT](https://qudt.org/) unit vocabulary, whose codes are the unit identifiers in IRI form.

name.description: The name of the custom unit system.

description.description: A description of the custom unit system.

url.description: URL of the specification or registry that defines the unit system.

code.title: Code
code.description: The code of the unit in the unit system.

url.title: URL
url.description: URL of the definition of the unit.

energyUnits.title: Energy Units
energyUnits.description: Units of energy. A single unit is defined so that energy figures are comparable without conversion.

meta:enum.kWh: Kilowatt hour, the energy delivered by one kilowatt of power for one hour, UCUM kW.h.

co2Units.title: CO2 Units
co2Units.description: Units of carbon dioxide equivalent. A single unit is defined so that emission figures are comparable without conversion.

meta:enum.tCO2eq: Tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, UCUM t{CO2eq}.

energyMeasure.title: Energy Measure
energyMeasure.description: A measure of energy. The unit is constrained to a standardized energy unit for accurate comparison and reporting.

co2Measure.title: CO2 Measure
co2Measure.description: A measure of carbon dioxide equivalent. The unit is constrained to a standardized unit for accurate environmental impact reporting.

bounds.title: Bounds
bounds.description: A pair of bounds on a numeric quantity, expressed in the unit of the quantity they accompany. At least one bound shall be given.

graphic.title: Graphic
graphic.description: A named graphic, such as a chart, plot, or diagram.

refId.description: An optional identifier which can be used to reference the graphic elsewhere using a `refId` or bom-link.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name of the graphic.

description.title: Description
description.description: A description of the graphic, such as what it depicts and how it was produced.

image.title: Graphic Image
image.description: The graphic, which may be a vector or raster image. Base64 encoding shall be specified for binary images.

graphicReference.title: Graphic Reference
graphicReference.description: A reference to a graphic defined elsewhere. A reference denotes an identical graphic.

ref.title: Reference
ref.description: Reference using bom-link or `refId` to the graphic.

graphics.title: Graphics
graphics.description: Graphics that support the record they are attached to, such as a chart, plot, or diagram. A graphic is attached to the record it supports; a graphic shared by several records is defined once and referenced.

graphicsCollection.title: Graphics Collection
graphicsCollection.description: A collection of graphics that represent various measurements.

description.title: Description
description.description: A description of this collection of graphics.

collection.title: Collection
collection.description: A collection of graphics. Items may be inline graphics or references to graphics defined elsewhere.

not.$comment: This schema is hollow: it is not referenced and only remains as a container for structures that are still in use. Itself must not be used for validation.

meta:enum.application: A software application. Refer to [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Application_software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Application_software) for information about applications.
meta:enum.framework: A software framework. Refer to [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_framework](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_framework) for information on how frameworks vary slightly from libraries.
meta:enum.library: A software library. Refer to [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Library_(computing)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Library_(computing)) for information about libraries. All third-party and open source reusable components will likely be a library. If the library also has key features of a framework, then it should be classified as a framework. If not, or is unknown, then specifying library is recommended.
meta:enum.container: A packaging and/or runtime format, not specific to any particular technology, which isolates software inside the container from software outside of a container through virtualization technology. Refer to [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OS-level_virtualization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OS-level_virtualization).
meta:enum.platform: A runtime environment that interprets or executes software. This may include runtimes such as those that execute bytecode, just-in-time compilers, interpreters, or low-code/no-code application platforms.
meta:enum.operating-system: A software operating system without regard to deployment model (i.e. installed on physical hardware, virtual machine, image, etc) Refer to [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operating_system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operating_system).
meta:enum.device: A hardware device such as a processor or chip-set. A hardware device containing firmware SHOULD include a component for the physical hardware itself and another component of type 'firmware' or 'operating-system' (whichever is relevant), describing information about the software running on the device. See also the list of [known device properties](https://github.com/CycloneDX/cyclonedx-property-taxonomy/blob/main/cdx/device.md).
meta:enum.device-driver: A special type of software that operates or controls a particular type of device. Refer to [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Device_driver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Device_driver).
meta:enum.firmware: A special type of software that provides low-level control over a device's hardware. Refer to [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firmware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firmware).
meta:enum.file: A computer file. Refer to [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_file](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_file) for information about files.
meta:enum.machine-learning-model: A model based on training data that can make predictions or decisions without being explicitly programmed to do so.
meta:enum.data: A collection of discrete values that convey information.
meta:enum.cryptographic-asset: A cryptographic asset including algorithms, protocols, certificates, keys, tokens, and secrets.
meta:enum.material: A physical substance in raw or processed form that is used to make, maintain, or repair an item, such as a metal, alloy, polymer, chemical, or other matter. Materials are commonly tracked for sourcing, provenance, and regulatory compliance. A finished physical item should be classified as 'device' instead.
meta:enum.service: A service, including microservices, function-as-a-service, and other types of network or intra-process services. Service-specific attributes, endpoints and the data profiles characterizing the data the service handles, apply exclusively to this component type.

type.title: Component Type
type.description: Specifies the type of component. For software components, classify as application if no more specific appropriate classification is available or cannot be determined for the component.

refId.title: Reference Identifier
refId.description:
An identifier which can be used to reference the component elsewhere in the document. Every `refId` shall be unique within the document.
Value should not start with the BOM-Link intro 'urn:cdx:' to avoid conflicts with BOM-Links.

origins.title: Component Origins
origins.description: The geographic origins of the component, each expressed as a distribution across one or more countries or subdivisions. Multiple origins are allowed, each calculated on a different basis.

group.title: Component Group
group.description: The grouping name or identifier. This will often be a shortened, single name of the company or project that produced the component, or the source package or domain name. Whitespace and special characters should be avoided. Examples include: apache, org.apache.commons, and apache.org.

name.title: Component Name
name.description: The name of the component. This will often be a shortened, single name of the component. Examples: commons-lang3 and jquery

version.title: Component Version
version.description:
The component version. The version should ideally comply with semantic versioning but is not enforced.
Must be used exclusively, either 'version' or 'versionRange', but not both.

versionRange.title: Component Version Range
versionRange.description:
For an external component, this specifies the accepted version range.
The value must adhere to the Package URL Version Range syntax (vers), as defined at <https://github.com/package-url/vers-spec
May only be used if `.isExternal` is set to `true`.
Must be used exclusively, either 'version' or 'versionRange', but not both.

isExternal.title: Component Is External
isExternal.description:
Determine whether this component is external.
An external component is one that is not part of an assembly, but is expected to be provided by the environment, regardless of the component's `.scope`. This setting can be useful for distinguishing which components are bundled with the product and which can be relied upon to be present in the deployment environment.
This may be set to `true` for runtime components only. For the subject of an inventory statement, it shall be `false`.

description.title: Component Description
description.description: Specifies a description for the component

meta:enum.required: The component is required for runtime
meta:enum.optional: The component is optional at runtime. Optional components are components that are not capable of being called due to them not being installed or otherwise accessible by any means. Components that are installed but due to configuration or other restrictions are prohibited from being called must be scoped as 'required'.
meta:enum.excluded: Components that are excluded provide the ability to document component usage for test and other non-runtime purposes. Excluded components are not reachable within a call graph at runtime.

scope.title: Component Scope
scope.description: Specifies the scope of the component. If scope is not specified, 'required' scope SHOULD be assumed by the consumer of the BOM.

pedigree.title: Component Pedigree
pedigree.description: Component pedigree is a way to document complex supply chain scenarios where components are created, distributed, modified, redistributed, combined with other components, etc. Pedigree supports viewing this complex chain from the beginning, the end, or anywhere in the middle. It also provides a way to document variants where the exact relation may not be known.

ancestors.title: Ancestors
ancestors.description: Describes zero or more components in which a component is derived from. This is commonly used to describe forks from existing projects where the forked version contains an ancestor node containing the original component it was forked from. For example, Component A is the original component. Component B is the component being used and documented in the BOM. However, Component B contains a pedigree node with a single ancestor documenting Component A - the original component from which Component B is derived from.

descendants.title: Descendants
descendants.description: Descendants are the exact opposite of ancestors. This provides a way to document all forks (and their forks) of an original or root component.

variants.title: Variants
variants.description: Variants describe relations where the relationship between the components is not known. For example, if Component A contains nearly identical code to Component B. They are both related, but it is unclear if one is derived from the other, or if they share a common ancestor.

commits.title: Commits
commits.description: A list of zero or more commits which provide a trail describing how the component deviates from an ancestor, descendant, or variant.

patches.title: Patches
patches.description: A list of zero or more patches describing how the component deviates from an ancestor, descendant, or variant. Patches may be complementary to commits or may be used in place of commits.

components.title: Components
components.description: A list of entries included in the parent component, including software, hardware, and services. Entries may be concrete components, references to components declared elsewhere, or component-choice wrappers expressing conditional or alternate relationships. This is not a dependency tree. It provides a way to specify a hierarchical representation of component assemblies, similar to system → subsystem → parts assembly in physical supply chains.

evidence.title: Evidence
evidence.description: Provides the ability to document evidence collected through various forms of extraction or analysis.

releaseNotes.title: Release Notes
releaseNotes.description: The release notes for the component. Either inline release notes or a reference using bom-link or `refId` to release notes defined elsewhere, such as in the definitions.

modelProperties.title: AI/ML Model Properties
modelProperties.description: Intrinsic technical characteristics of a machine learning model. This object SHOULD be specified for any component of type `machine-learning-model` and shall not be specified for other component types.

data.title: Data
data.description: This object SHOULD be specified for any component of type `data` and must not be specified for other component types.

classification.title: Classification
classification.description: Hierarchical classification of the item, with optional taxonomy codes from external standards. This object may only be specified for components of type `device` or `material` and shall not be specified for other component types.

boardLocation.title: Board Location
boardLocation.description: Placement of the item on a printed circuit board, panel, or assembly. This object may only be specified for components of type `device` and shall not be specified for other component types.

deviceType.title: Device Type
deviceType.description: Package or mounting style of the physical item, expressed as a predefined device type or a custom device type. This object may only be specified for components of type `device` and shall not be specified for other component types.

leadTime.title: Lead Time
leadTime.description: Supplier lead time for procuring the item. This object may only be specified for components of type `device` or `material` and shall not be specified for other component types.

materialForm.title: Material Form
materialForm.description: Physical form in which the material is supplied, expressed as a predefined material form or a custom material form. This object may only be specified for components of type `material` and shall not be specified for other component types.

quantity.title: Quantity
quantity.description: The quantity of the item in the context in which it is declared, such as the number of identical parts within the enclosing assembly or the amount of material in the described lot. This object may only be specified for components of type `device` or `material` and shall not be specified for other component types.

certifications.title: Certifications
certifications.description: Certifications held by or applicable to the component. Each entry is either an inline certification or a reference using bom-link or `refId` to a certification defined elsewhere, such as in the definitions. Applicable to components of any type, hardware and software alike.

endpoints.title: Endpoints
endpoints.description: The endpoint URIs of the service. Multiple endpoints are allowed. May only be used for components of type `service`.

dataProfiles.title: Data Profiles
dataProfiles.description: The data handled by the service, characterized by data profiles. Each entry is either an inline profile object or a reference using bom-link or `refId` to a previously declared profile, typically declared in the definitions. May only be used for components of type `service`. Data movement is intentionally not expressed here: flow direction, sources, destinations, authentication, and boundary crossings are modelled via blueprint flows, assets, and boundaries, which reference this component by `refId`.

allOf.description: Requirement: ensure that `version` and `versionRange` are mutually exclusive.
Requirement: 'versionRange' must not be present when 'isExternal' is `false`.
Requirement: `classification`, `leadTime`, and `quantity` may only be present when `type` is `device` or `material`.
Requirement: `boardLocation` and `deviceType` may only be present when `type` is `device`.
Requirement: `materialForm` may only be present when `type` is `material`.

allOf.title: Service Requirement
allOf.description: Requirement: endpoints and dataProfiles may only be used for components of type `service`.

componentEntry.title: Component Entry
componentEntry.description: An entry in a components array. A concrete component, a reference to a component declared elsewhere, or a component-choice wrapper that expresses a conditional or alternate relationship between two or more entries. An entry with a `ref` property is a reference; an entry whose `type` is `component-choice` is a choice; any other entry is a component.

componentChoice.title: Component Choice
componentChoice.description: A wrapper that expresses a conditional or alternate relationship between two or more components. Use to model approved alternates, multi-sourced parts, build variants, and required component groups in physical device bills of materials.

type.title: Type
type.description: Discriminator for a component-choice entry. The value shall be the literal string `component-choice`.

refId.title: Reference Identifier
refId.description:
An identifier which can be used to reference the component-choice elsewhere in the document. Every `refId` shall be unique within the document.
Value should not start with the BOM-Link intro 'urn:cdx:' to avoid conflicts with BOM-Links.

name.title: Name
name.description: A display name for the choice. Typically corresponds to a reference designator, a design intent name, or a description of the role the chosen component fulfils.

description.title: Description
description.description: A description of the choice and the rationale behind the alternates.

meta:enum.OR: Any non-empty subset of the contained components may be installed. Use for approved alternates where more than one may legitimately appear in a given instance.
meta:enum.XOR: Exactly one of the contained components is installed in any single instance. Use for approved alternates that are mutually exclusive per instance, while the population of units may include multiple alternates across sourcing.
meta:enum.AND: All of the contained components are installed together as a group. Use for tightly coupled component sets such as a transceiver and its required matching balun.

operator.title: Operator
operator.description: The logical relationship between the contained components.

components.title: Components
components.description: Two or more alternate or grouped entries. Each entry may itself be a component-choice to express nested alternates, such as a choice between kits.

version.description: A single disjunctive version identifier for a component.

versionRange.description: A version range specified in Package-URL Version Range syntax (vers) which is defined at https://github.com/package-url/vers-spec

copyrightText.title: Component Copyright
copyrightText.description: A copyright notice informing users of the underlying claims to copyright ownership in a published work.

componentEvidence.title: Evidence
componentEvidence.description: Provides the ability to document evidence collected through various forms of extraction or analysis.

identity.title: Identity Evidence
identity.description: Evidence that substantiates the identity of the component, including how each identity was determined, the confidence, and the tools and parties involved.

occurrences.title: Occurrences
occurrences.description: Evidence of individual instances of a component spread across multiple locations.

callStacks.description: Evidence of the components use through one or more call stacks.

licenses.title: License Evidence
licenses.description: Evidence that substantiates the licenses detected in the component, including how each license was detected, the confidence, the tools and parties involved, and where it was found.

copyright.title: Copyright Evidence
copyright.description: Evidence that substantiates the copyright statements detected in the component, including how each was detected, the confidence, the tools and parties involved, and where it was found.

licenseEvidence.title: License Evidence
licenseEvidence.description: A detected license, together with how it was detected, the confidence in the detection, the tools and parties involved, and where it was found.

refId.title: Reference Identifier
refId.description:
An identifier which can be used to reference this license evidence elsewhere in the document. Every `refId` shall be unique within the document.
Value should not start with the BOM-Link intro 'urn:cdx:' to avoid conflicts with BOM-Links.

license.title: License
license.description: The detected license, expressed as a single SPDX license identifier or a named license.

expression.title: License Expression
expression.description: The detected license, expressed as an SPDX license expression.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: The overall confidence of the detection from 0 to 1, where 1 is 100% confidence.

methods.title: Methods
methods.description: The methods used to detect the license.

tools.title: Tools
tools.description: The tools that detected the license, referenced by `refId`.

occurrences.title: Occurrences
occurrences.description: The locations at which the license was detected, for example a license file or a source header.

assertion.description: The parties involved in detecting the license and the perspective from which the detection is asserted.

timestamp.title: Timestamp
timestamp.description: The date and time at which the license was detected.

copyrightEvidence.title: Copyright Evidence
copyrightEvidence.description: A detected copyright statement, together with how it was detected, the confidence in the detection, the tools and parties involved, and where it was found.

refId.title: Reference Identifier
refId.description:
An identifier which can be used to reference this copyright evidence elsewhere in the document. Every `refId` shall be unique within the document.
Value should not start with the BOM-Link intro 'urn:cdx:' to avoid conflicts with BOM-Links.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: The overall confidence of the detection from 0 to 1, where 1 is 100% confidence.

methods.title: Methods
methods.description: The methods used to detect the copyright statement.

tools.title: Tools
tools.description: The tools that detected the copyright statement, referenced by `refId`.

occurrences.title: Occurrences
occurrences.description: The locations at which the copyright statement was detected.

assertion.description: The parties involved in detecting the copyright statement and the perspective from which the detection is asserted.

timestamp.title: Timestamp
timestamp.description: The date and time at which the copyright statement was detected.

componentIdentityEvidence.title: Identity Evidence
componentIdentityEvidence.description: Evidence that substantiates the identity of a component.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: The overall confidence of the evidence from 0 - 1, where 1 is 100% confidence.

concludedValue.title: Concluded Value
concludedValue.description: The value of the scheme that has been concluded based on the aggregate of all methods (if available).

methods.title: Methods
methods.description: The methods used to extract and/or analyze the evidence.

tools.title: Tools
tools.description: The object in the BOM identified by its `refId`. This is often a component or service but may be any object type supporting `refId`s. Tools used for analysis should already be defined in the BOM, such as in the metadata tools, an inventory, or the definitions.

assertion.description: The party asserting this identity determination and the perspective from which it is made. Attribution lets identity determinations from different parties, such as a supplier and a downstream analyzer, coexist and be weighed.

timestamp.title: Timestamp
timestamp.description: The date and time at which this identity determination was made or last held to be valid.

refId.title: Reference Identifier
refId.description:
An identifier which can be used to reference the dataset elsewhere in the document. Every `refId` shall be unique within the document.
Value should not start with the BOM-Link intro 'urn:cdx:' to avoid conflicts with BOM-Links.

type.title: Type of Data
type.description: The general theme or subject matter of the data being specified.

meta:enum.source-code: Any type of code, code snippet, or data-as-code.
meta:enum.configuration: Parameters or settings that may be used by other components.
meta:enum.definition: Data that can be used to create new instances of what the definition defines.
meta:enum.other: Any other type of data that does not fit into existing definitions.

name.title: Dataset Name
name.description: The name of the dataset.

contents.title: Data Contents
contents.description: The contents or references to the contents of the data being described.

sensitiveData.title: Sensitive Data
sensitiveData.description: A description of any sensitive data in a dataset.

description.title: Dataset Description
description.description: A description of the dataset. Can describe size of dataset, whether it's used for source code, training, testing, or validation, etc.

agility.title: Agility
agility.description: Properties describing how this component's configuration was determined and how a change to it can be applied. These properties support change management and, for cryptographic assets, cryptographic-agility.

configurationSource.title: Configuration Source
configurationSource.description: Describes how this component's configuration was determined. Values are roughly ordered from least to most agile, the ordering is approximate.

meta:enum.hardcoded: The configuration is fixed in code or firmware and is not intended to be changed.
meta:enum.product-default: The configuration is inherited from product or vendor defaults and can typically be overridden.
meta:enum.administrator-configured: The configuration is explicitly set by an administrator through external configuration.
meta:enum.policy-managed: The configuration is determined by a policy or governance engine.
meta:enum.unknown: The configuration source is not known.

negotiated.title: Negotiated
negotiated.description: Indicates whether the effective configuration is selected at runtime through negotiation with one or multiple peers, such as a protocol handshake, rather than being statically fixed. This is orthogonal to `configurationSource`, which describes how the permitted configuration was determined.

configurationRef.title: Configuration Reference
configurationRef.description: The `refId` of the configuration that determines this component's configuration. Typically points to a component of type 'data' whose data type is 'configuration'.

changeMechanism.title: Change Mechanism
changeMechanism.description: The step or steps required to apply a change to this component's configuration. When more than one value is present, all are required (for example, a software update followed by a restart). Values are roughly ordered from least to most disruptive. Use a single value of 'not-possible' when the configuration cannot be changed.

meta:enum.not-possible: The configuration cannot be changed through any supported means.
meta:enum.hardware-replacement: The change requires replacing or adding hardware.
meta:enum.firmware-update: The change requires a firmware update.
meta:enum.software-update: The change requires a software or package update.
meta:enum.restart-required: The change requires restarting software or service processes.
meta:enum.runtime-config: The change can be applied at runtime without a restart.
meta:enum.unknown: The change mechanism is not known.

identifiers.title: Identifiers
identifiers.description: Identifiers asserted by one or more parties to identify this component. Each entry groups one or more identity claims by the party asserting them. Identifiers carry positive claims of identity. For unverified or inferred identity data, use evidence.

identifier.title: Identifier
identifier.description: A set of identifiers attributed to a single asserting party.

party.title: Asserting Party
party.description: Reference using bom-link or `refId` to the party making the identity assertion.

identities.title: Identities
identities.description: The discrete identity claims asserted by the party.

identity.title: Identity
identity.description: A single identity claim, pairing a typed identifier scheme with the value asserted under that scheme.

identityScheme.title: Identifier Scheme
identityScheme.description: The scheme under which an identifier is asserted. Either a predefined value or a custom scheme described by name and description.

meta:enum.purl: Package-URL identifier, conforming to the Package-URL specification.
meta:enum.cpe: Common Platform Enumeration name, conforming to NIST Interagency Report 7695.
meta:enum.swid: Software Identification tag identifier, conforming to ISO/IEC 19770-2.
meta:enum.omniborid: OmniBOR Artifact Identifier, also known as a gitoid.
meta:enum.epc-rfid: Electronic Product Code - RFID (EPC Tag Data Standard)
meta:enum.gtin-14: Global Trade Identification Number (GTIN / EAN/UCC-14 or ITF-14)
meta:enum.mpn: Manufacturer Part Number, assigned by the original manufacturer.
meta:enum.part-number: Part number assigned by a distributor, integrator, or operator.
meta:enum.model-number: Product model number assigned by the manufacturer.
meta:enum.sku: Stock Keeping Unit, assigned by a seller or distributor.
meta:enum.serial-number: Unique identifier for an individual instance of a product.
meta:enum.asset-tag: Asset tag assigned by the owning or operating organization.
meta:enum.udi-di: Unique Device Identifier, Device Identifier portion, conforming to ISO/IEC 15459 and applicable regulatory frameworks.
meta:enum.udi-pi: Unique Device Identifier, Production Identifier portion, conforming to ISO/IEC 15459 and applicable regulatory frameworks.
meta:enum.fcc-id: United States Federal Communications Commission equipment identifier.
meta:enum.imei: International Mobile Equipment Identity, conforming to 3GPP TS 23.003.
meta:enum.tei: Transparency Exchange Identifier conforming to the Transparency Exchange API specification.

oneOf.title: Custom Identifier Scheme
oneOf.description: A custom identifier scheme not represented in the predefined taxonomy.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name of the custom identifier scheme.

description.title: Description
description.description: A description of the custom identifier scheme.

componentReference.title: Component Reference
componentReference.description: A reference to a component declared elsewhere, such as in the definitions registry, in another position of the same document, or in another document via BOM-Link. A reference includes the referenced component exactly as declared: every position that references the same component includes an identical component. Where the inclusion context differs, such as a different scope or quantity, declare the component inline instead.

ref.title: Reference
ref.description: Reference using bom-link or `refId` to the component.

inventories.title: Inventories
inventories.description: The inventories of the subjects that the document describes. Each entry declares one subject and lists the entries included in it.

inventory.title: Inventory
inventory.description: The declared inventory of one subject: the entries included in the subject. The completeness of the list is asserted through compositions.

refId.title: Reference Identifier
refId.description: An identifier which can be used to reference the inventory elsewhere in the document. Every `refId` shall be unique within the document.

subject.title: Subject
subject.description: The subject whose inventory this statement declares. Either a concrete component or a reference using bom-link or `refId` to a component declared elsewhere, such as in the definitions.

components.description: The entries included in the subject. Entries may be concrete components, references to components declared elsewhere, or component-choice wrappers.

signatures.description: Enveloped signatures over the inventory statement. A signature binds reference entries by their identifiers; the content of a referenced component is covered by the hashes or signatures on the referenced component itself.

measurements.title: Measurements
measurements.description: Measured quantities of the component. An energy consumption records the energy consumed by a lifecycle activity of the component together with its providers and carbon dioxide equivalent. A performance metric records a benchmark or evaluation result of the component. Each record may carry graphics that support it.

lifecycleActivity.title: Lifecycle Activity
lifecycleActivity.description: An activity in the lifecycle of a component that consumes energy, such as the manufacture of a device or the training of a model. Use the custom option for activities not covered by the predefined values.

meta:enum.design: Design, including problem framing, goal definition, and algorithm or architecture selection.
meta:enum.data-collection: Data acquisition, including search, selection, and transfer.
meta:enum.data-preparation: Data preparation, including data cleaning, labelling, and conversion.
meta:enum.training: Model building, training, and generalized tuning.
meta:enum.fine-tuning: Refining a trained model to produce desired outputs for a given problem space.
meta:enum.validation: Validation, including output evaluation and testing.
meta:enum.manufacturing: Manufacture of a physical item, including fabrication and assembly.
meta:enum.transport: Transport of a physical item between sites.
meta:enum.deployment: Deployment to a target hosting infrastructure or site.
meta:enum.operation: Operation of a deployed component over a stated period.
meta:enum.inference: Generating an output response from a hosted model from a set of inputs.
meta:enum.end-of-life: Decommissioning, recycling, or disposal of a component.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name of the custom activity.

description.title: Description
description.description: A description of the custom activity.

energyConsumption.title: Energy Consumption
energyConsumption.description: The energy consumption incurred for a specific lifecycle activity of the component.

activity.title: Activity
activity.description: The lifecycle activity that incurred the energy consumption.

description.title: Description
description.description: A description of the energy consumption, including its scope and how it was measured or estimated.

formula.title: Formula Reference
formula.description: References using bom-link or `refId` a formula, workflow, or task, defined in formulation, that captures the process which incurred this energy consumption, for example a training workflow or a manufacturing run.

energyProviders.title: Energy Providers
energyProviders.description: The providers of the energy consumed by the activity.

activityEnergyCost.title: Activity Energy Cost
activityEnergyCost.description: The total energy cost associated with the activity.

co2CostEquivalent.title: CO2 Equivalent Cost
co2CostEquivalent.description: The carbon dioxide equivalent cost of the total energy cost.

co2CostOffset.title: CO2 Cost Offset
co2CostOffset.description: The carbon dioxide offset credited against the carbon dioxide equivalent cost.

graphics.title: Graphics
graphics.description: Graphics that support the energy consumption, such as a load profile or a meter reading.

externalReferences.title: External References
externalReferences.description: External references to resources that are relevant to the energy consumption but are not included with the BOM.

properties.description: Provides the ability to document name-value pairs for the energy consumption. Property names of interest to the general public are encouraged to be registered in the [CycloneDX Property Taxonomy](https://github.com/CycloneDX/cyclonedx-property-taxonomy). Formal registration is optional.

energySource.title: Energy Source
energySource.description: The source of the energy provided by an energy provider. Use the custom option for sources not covered by the predefined values.

meta:enum.oil: Energy produced from petroleum products, primarily crude oil and its derivative fuel oils.
meta:enum.natural-gas: Energy produced from hydrocarbon gases, including natural gas, ethane, and propane.
meta:enum.nuclear: Energy produced from the cores of atoms through nuclear fission or fusion.
meta:enum.geothermal: Energy produced from heat within the earth.
meta:enum.biofuel: Energy produced from liquid fuels derived from biomass feedstocks.
meta:enum.biomass: Energy produced from solid organic materials such as wood, agricultural crops, or organic waste.
meta:enum.hydrogen: Energy produced from hydrogen fuel in fuel cells or combustion.
meta:enum.tidal: Energy produced from the rise and fall of ocean tides and tidal currents.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name of the custom energy source.

description.title: Description
description.description: A description of the custom energy source.

energyProvider.title: Energy Provider
energyProvider.description: The provider of energy consumed by a lifecycle activity of the component.

refId.title: Reference Identifier
refId.description: An optional identifier which can be used to reference the energy provider elsewhere using a `refId` or bom-link.

description.title: Description
description.description: A description of the energy provider.

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: The party that provides the consumed energy, typically an organization.

energySource.title: Energy Source
energySource.description: The source of the provided energy.

energyProvided.title: Energy Provided
energyProvided.description: The energy provided by the energy source for the associated activity.

externalReferences.title: External References
externalReferences.description: External references to resources that are relevant to the energy provider but are not included with the BOM.

properties.title: Properties
properties.description: Provides the ability to document name-value pairs for the energy provider. Property names of interest to the general public are encouraged to be registered in the [CycloneDX Property Taxonomy](https://github.com/CycloneDX/cyclonedx-property-taxonomy). Formal registration is optional.

compositions.title: Compositions
compositions.description: Completeness assertions for enumerations in the document, such as the components of a subject, the dependencies of a component, or the vulnerability disclosure for a subject.

composition.title: Composition
composition.description: A completeness assertion: for each target, the enumeration named by `kind` is as complete as `aggregate` states.

refId.title: Reference Identifier
refId.description:
An identifier which can be used to reference the composition elsewhere in the document. Every `refId` shall be unique within the document.
Value should not start with the BOM-Link intro 'urn:cdx:' to avoid conflicts with BOM-Links.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: The enumeration the completeness assertion applies to. Either a predefined kind or a custom kind described by name and description.

meta:enum.components: The components included in each target: the entries of an inventory statement or of a nested assembly. The assertion does not cascade to the assemblies of nested entries.
meta:enum.dependencies: The direct dependencies of each target. The assertion does not cascade to transitive dependencies.
meta:enum.vulnerabilities: The vulnerability disclosure for each target.
meta:enum.licenses: The licenses that apply to each target. A complete assertion with no licenses on the target states that the target has no licenses.
meta:enum.certifications: The certifications held by each target. A complete assertion with no certifications on the target states that the target holds no certifications.

oneOf.title: Custom Kind
oneOf.description: A custom completeness kind not represented in the predefined taxonomy.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name of the custom kind.

description.title: Description
description.description: A description of the custom kind.

aggregate.title: Aggregate
aggregate.description: Specifies an aggregate type that describes how complete the relationship is.

targets.title: Targets
targets.description: References using bom-link or `refId` to the objects whose enumeration the assertion describes. The document itself may be a target, referenced by a BOM-Link document reference.

meta:enum.complete: The enumeration is complete. No additional items are known to exist.
meta:enum.incomplete: The enumeration is incomplete. Additional items are known or expected to exist.
meta:enum.incomplete-first-party-only: The enumeration is incomplete. Only first-party items are represented.
meta:enum.incomplete-first-party-proprietary-only: The enumeration is incomplete. Only first-party items are represented, limited specifically to those that are proprietary.
meta:enum.incomplete-first-party-opensource-only: The enumeration is incomplete. Only first-party items are represented, limited specifically to those that are open source.
meta:enum.incomplete-third-party-only: The enumeration is incomplete. Only third-party items are represented.
meta:enum.incomplete-third-party-proprietary-only: The enumeration is incomplete. Only third-party items are represented, limited specifically to those that are proprietary.
meta:enum.incomplete-third-party-opensource-only: The enumeration is incomplete. Only third-party items are represented, limited specifically to those that are open source.
meta:enum.unknown: The enumeration may be complete or incomplete. This usually signifies a best-effort attempt whose completeness is inconclusive.

controls.title: Controls
controls.description:
The safeguards and countermeasures that are recommended or in place.
 Controls may be declared on their own for governance, risk, and compliance use cases, or referenced from threats, trust boundaries, and risk responses.

control.title: Control
control.description: A safeguard or countermeasure that protects systems, data, or operations. A control binds the elements that implement it to the requirements it satisfies, and records its implementation status and assessed effectiveness.

refId.description: An identifier which can be used to reference the control elsewhere using a `refId` or bom-link.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name of the control.

description.title: Description
description.description: A description of the control.

category.title: Category
category.description: The category of the control. Use the custom option for a category specific to an organization's taxonomy.

meta:enum.preventive: Prevents an unwanted event from occurring.
meta:enum.detective: Identifies and records that an unwanted event has occurred or is occurring.
meta:enum.corrective: Remedies the condition that allowed an unwanted event.
meta:enum.compensating: Provides an alternative safeguard where a primary control is not feasible.
meta:enum.deterrent: Discourages an actor from attempting an unwanted action.
meta:enum.recovery: Restores operations after an unwanted event.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name of the custom category.

description.title: Description
description.description: A description of the custom category.

status.title: Status
status.description: The implementation status of the control.

appliesTo.title: Applies To
appliesTo.description: References using bom-link or `refId` to the elements the control protects, such as components, services, zones, or boundaries. A control without this property applies to the organization or system as a whole.

implementedBy.title: Implemented By
implementedBy.description: References using bom-link or `refId` to the components, services, formulation workflows, or parties that implement the control.

satisfies.title: Satisfies
satisfies.description: References using bom-link or `refId` to the requirements the control satisfies, including requirements defined within standards.

effectiveness.title: Effectiveness
effectiveness.description: The assessed effectiveness of the control.

owner.description: The party accountable for the control. May be an inline party object or a reference to a previously declared party.

implementationStatus.title: Implementation Status
implementationStatus.description: The implementation status of a control or response. Use the custom option for a status specific to an organization's process.

meta:enum.recommended: Suggested by a producer, standard, or assessor. Not yet entered into the adopting organization's decision process.
meta:enum.proposed: Entered into the adopting organization's decision process but not yet approved.
meta:enum.rejected: Considered and declined, with no intent to implement.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name of the custom status.

description.title: Description
description.description: A description of the custom status.

effectiveness.title: Effectiveness
effectiveness.description: The measured or assessed effectiveness of a control or response.

percentage.description: Effectiveness as a decimal from 0 to 1.

cryptoProperties.title: Cryptographic Properties
cryptoProperties.description: Cryptographic assets have properties that uniquely define them and that make them actionable for further reasoning. As an example, it makes a difference if one knows the algorithm family (e.g. AES) or the specific variant or instantiation (e.g. AES-128-GCM). This is because the security level and the algorithm primitive (authenticated encryption) are only defined by the definition of the algorithm variant. The presence of a weak cryptographic algorithm like SHA1 vs. HMAC-SHA1 also makes a difference.

assetType.title: Asset Type
assetType.description: Cryptographic assets occur in several forms. Algorithms and protocols are most commonly implemented in specialized cryptographic libraries. They may, however, also be 'hardcoded' in software components. Certificates and related cryptographic material like keys, tokens, secrets or passwords are other cryptographic assets to be modelled.

meta:enum.algorithm: Mathematical function commonly used for data encryption, authentication, and digital signatures.
meta:enum.certificate: An electronic document that is used to provide the identity or validate a public key.
meta:enum.protocol: A set of rules and guidelines that govern the behavior and communication with each other.
