vulnerability.description: Defines a weakness in a component or service that could be exploited or triggered by a threat source.

refId.title: Reference Identifier
refId.description:
An identifier which can be used to reference the vulnerability elsewhere in the document. Every `refId` shall be unique within the document.
Value should not start with the BOM-Link intro 'urn:cdx:' to avoid conflicts with BOM-Links.

id.title: ID
id.description: The identifier that uniquely identifies the vulnerability.

source.description: The source that published the vulnerability.

references.title: References
references.description: Zero or more pointers to vulnerabilities that are the equivalent of the vulnerability specified. Often times, the same vulnerability may exist in multiple sources of vulnerability intelligence, but have different identifiers. References provide a way to correlate vulnerabilities across multiple sources of vulnerability intelligence.

id.title: ID
id.description: An identifier that uniquely identifies the vulnerability.

source.description: The source that published the vulnerability.

ratings.title: Ratings
ratings.description: List of vulnerability ratings. Consumers should consider ratings in prioritization decisions; source ratings may differ and aid prioritization.

weaknesses.description: The weaknesses that give rise to this vulnerability.

description.title: Description
description.description: A description of the vulnerability as provided by the source.

detail.title: Details
detail.description: If available, an in-depth description of the vulnerability as provided by the source organization. Details often include information useful in understanding root cause.

recommendation.title: Recommendation
recommendation.description: Recommendations of how the vulnerability can be remediated or mitigated.

workaround.title: Workarounds
workaround.description: A bypass, usually temporary, of the vulnerability that reduces its likelihood and/or impact. Workarounds often involve changes to configuration or deployments.

proofOfConcept.title: Proof of Concept
proofOfConcept.description: Evidence used to reproduce the vulnerability.

reproductionSteps.title: Steps to Reproduce
reproductionSteps.description: Precise steps to reproduce the vulnerability.

environment.title: Environment
environment.description: A description of the environment in which reproduction was possible.

supportingMaterial.title: Supporting Material
supportingMaterial.description: Supporting material that helps in reproducing or understanding how reproduction is possible. This may include screenshots, payloads, and PoC exploit code.

advisories.title: Advisories
advisories.description: Published advisories of the vulnerability if provided.

created.title: Created
created.description: The date and time (timestamp) when the vulnerability record was created in the vulnerability database.

published.title: Published
published.description: The date and time (timestamp) when the vulnerability record was first published.

updated.title: Updated
updated.description: The date and time (timestamp) when the vulnerability record was last updated.

rejected.title: Rejected
rejected.description: The date and time (timestamp) when the vulnerability record was rejected (if applicable).

credits.title: Credits
credits.description: Individuals or organizations credited with the discovery of the vulnerability.

organizations.title: Organizations
organizations.description: The organizations credited with vulnerability discovery.

individuals.title: Individuals
individuals.description: The individuals, not associated with organizations, that are credited with vulnerability discovery.

tools.title: Tools
tools.description: The tool(s) used to identify, confirm, or score the vulnerability.

components.title: Components
components.description: A list of components used as tools. This may include software, hardware, and services such as microservices and function-as-a-service.

analysis.title: Impact Analysis
analysis.description: An assessment of the impact and exploitability of the vulnerability.

mitigatingControls.title: Mitigating Controls
mitigatingControls.description: References using bom-link or `refId` to the controls that prevent or reduce the exploitability or impact of the vulnerability. Substantiates justifications such as protected_by_mitigating_control, protected_at_perimeter, and protected_at_runtime.

response.title: Response
response.description: A response to the vulnerability by the manufacturer, supplier, or project responsible for the affected component or service. More than one response is allowed. Responses are strongly encouraged for vulnerabilities where the analysis state is exploitable.

meta:enum.update: Update to a different revision or release
meta:enum.rollback: Revert to a previous revision or release

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: Detailed description of the impact including methods used during assessment. If a vulnerability is not exploitable, this field should include specific details on why the component or service is not impacted by this vulnerability.

firstIssued.title: First Issued
firstIssued.description: The date and time (timestamp) when the analysis was first issued.

lastUpdated.title: Last Updated
lastUpdated.description: The date and time (timestamp) when the analysis was last updated.

evidence.description: Evidence collected through extraction or analysis that substantiates the presence, absence, or exploitability of the vulnerability in the affected components. Evidence supports both positive determinations, such as a confirmed exploitable finding, and negative determinations, such as a `not_affected` conclusion, and complements the impact analysis and the proof of concept.

ref.title: Reference
ref.description: References a component or service by the objects `refId`

versions.title: Versions
versions.description: Zero or more individual versions or range of versions.

version.title: Version
version.description: A single version of a component or service.

range.title: Version Range
range.description: A version range specified in Package URL Version Range syntax (vers) which is defined at https://github.com/package-url/vers-spec

status.title: Status
status.description: The vulnerability status for the version or range of versions.

affects.title: Affects
affects.description: The components or services that are affected by the vulnerability.

advisory.title: Advisory
advisory.description: Title and location where advisory information can be obtained. An advisory is a notification of a threat to a component, service, or system.

url.title: URL
url.description: Location where the advisory can be obtained.

severity.title: Severity
severity.description: Textual representation of the severity of the vulnerability adopted by the analysis method. If the analysis method uses values other than what is provided, the user is expected to translate appropriately.

scoreMethod.title: Method
scoreMethod.description: Specifies the severity or risk scoring methodology or standard used. Use the custom option for methodologies not listed.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name of the custom scoring methodology.

description.title: Description
description.description: A description of the custom scoring methodology.

impactAnalysisState.title: Impact Analysis State
impactAnalysisState.description: Declares the current state of an occurrence of a vulnerability, after automated or manual analysis.

meta:enum.resolved_with_pedigree: The vulnerability has been remediated and evidence of the changes are provided in the affected components pedigree containing verifiable commit history and/or diff(s).
meta:enum.exploitable: The vulnerability may be directly or indirectly exploitable.
meta:enum.false_positive: The vulnerability is not specific to the component or service and was falsely identified or associated.
meta:enum.not_affected: The component or service is not affected by the vulnerability. Justification should be specified for all not_affected cases.

impactAnalysisJustification.title: Impact Analysis Justification
impactAnalysisJustification.description: The rationale of why the impact analysis state was asserted.

meta:enum.code_not_present: The code has been removed or tree-shaked.
meta:enum.code_not_reachable: The vulnerable code is not invoked at runtime.
meta:enum.requires_configuration: Exploitability requires a configurable option to be set/unset.
meta:enum.requires_dependency: Exploitability requires a dependency that is not present.
meta:enum.requires_environment: Exploitability requires a certain environment which is not present.
meta:enum.protected_by_compiler: Exploitability requires a compiler flag to be set/unset.
meta:enum.protected_at_perimeter: Attacks are blocked at physical, logical, or network perimeter.
meta:enum.protected_by_mitigating_control: Preventive measures have been implemented that reduce the likelihood or impact of the vulnerability, or both. The controls may be referenced using the mitigatingControls property.

rating.title: Rating
rating.description: Defines the severity or risk ratings of a vulnerability.

source.description: The source that calculated the severity or risk rating of the vulnerability.

score.title: Score
score.description: The numerical score of the rating, on the scale defined by the method. Methods that do not produce a single score on that scale record their values in `measures` instead.

measures.title: Measures
measures.description: Named values produced by the scoring method. Methods that emit more than one value, or a value on a scale unlike the primary score, record each value here rather than in `score`. Each measure name shall appear at most once within a rating.

severity.description: Textual representation of the severity that corresponds to the numerical score of the rating.

methodVersion.title: Method Version
methodVersion.description: The version or revision of the scoring method that produced this rating, for methods that version themselves independently of the value recorded in `method`.

vector.title: Vector
vector.description: Textual representation of the metric values used to score the vulnerability

timestamp.title: Timestamp
timestamp.description: The date and time the rating was produced or observed. Relevant to methods whose scores are recalculated on a schedule.

justification.title: Justification
justification.description: A reason for rating the vulnerability as it was

allOf.$comment: The Exploit Prediction Scoring System reports probabilities and ranks rather than a score on the severity scale that `score` carries, so its values are recorded as named measures. Constraining the form keeps an EPSS probability from being read or ordered as though it were a severity score.

ratingMeasure.title: Rating Measure
ratingMeasure.description: A named value produced by a scoring method. The set of names a method emits is defined by that method.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name of the measure, given as a predefined name or as a custom name defined by the scoring method.

meta:enum.probability: The likelihood of the scored outcome within the period defined by the method, expressed as a decimal from 0 to 1.
meta:enum.percentile: The proportion of the scored population at or below this subject, expressed as a decimal from 0 to 1.
meta:enum.confidence: The degree of certainty in the score, expressed as a decimal from 0 to 1.
meta:enum.rank: The position of the subject within the scored population.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name of the custom measure.

description.title: Description
description.description: A description of the custom measure.

value.title: Value
value.description: The numeric value of the measure.

vulnerabilitySource.title: Source
vulnerabilitySource.description: The source of vulnerability information. This is often the organization that published the vulnerability.

url.title: URL
url.description: The url of the vulnerability documentation as provided by the source.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name of the source.

affectedStatus.description: The vulnerability status of a given version or range of versions of a product. The statuses 'affected' and 'unaffected' indicate that the version is affected or unaffected by the vulnerability. The status 'unknown' indicates that it is unknown or unspecified whether the given version is affected. There can be many reasons for an 'unknown' status, including that an investigation has not been undertaken or that a vendor has not disclosed the status.

meta:enum.affected: The version is affected by the vulnerability.
meta:enum.unaffected: The version is not affected by the vulnerability.
meta:enum.unknown: It is unknown (or unspecified) whether the given version is affected.

vulnerabilityEvidence.title: Vulnerability Evidence
vulnerabilityEvidence.description: Documents evidence collected through various forms of extraction or analysis that substantiates the presence, absence, or exploitability of the vulnerability. The structure mirrors component evidence so that determination, location, and call stack information are expressed consistently across the specification.

presence.title: Presence
presence.description: Evidence that substantiates the presence or absence of the vulnerability, and, where determined, the degree to which it is exploitable. Each entry records an independent determination, its confidence, and the methods that produced it.

occurrences.title: Occurrences
occurrences.description: Evidence of individual locations at which the vulnerability manifests, for example, an affected file, line, byte offset, or symbol. A vulnerability can occur at more than one location.

callStacks.description: Evidence of the vulnerability through one or more call stacks or data flow paths, for example, the propagation of untrusted data from an entry point to a sensitive operation. A vulnerability may be reachable by more than one path.

data.title: Supporting Data
data.description: Supporting material that records or reproduces the evidence, for example scanner output, request and response transcripts, the prompt and completion pairs of a language model assessment, payloads, or screenshots. Each item is labelled so that consumers can identify the kind of material without inspecting its contents.

presenceEvidence.title: Presence Evidence
presenceEvidence.description: A single, attributable determination about the presence, absence, or exploitability of the vulnerability, together with the confidence in that determination and the methods used to reach it. Determinations are perspectival: several entries may concern the same reference from different vantages, each attributed through `assertion`, so a supplier assertion of unaffected and a consumer assertion of affected can coexist. The vulnerability-level `analysis` remains the document author's consolidated impact analysis; a determination concerning the same subject should be consistent with `analysis` or, where it differs, should be attributed to a different perspective. `status` corresponds to `analysis.state`, `justification` to `analysis.justification`, and `exploitability` refines them with a graduated level of substantiation.

refId.title: Reference Identifier
refId.description:
An identifier which can be used to reference this evidence elsewhere in the document, for example from an attestation claim that relies upon it. Every `refId` shall be unique within the document.
Value should not start with the BOM-Link intro 'urn:cdx:' to avoid conflicts with BOM-Links.

ref.title: Reference
ref.description: References the affected component or service, by `refId`, to which this determination applies. The reference should correspond to an entry in `affects`. When omitted, the determination applies to the vulnerability generally.

status.title: Status
status.description: The determination of whether the referenced subject is affected, unaffected, or of unknown status based on this evidence. This enables evidence to be recorded in both positive and negative contexts. It corresponds to the vulnerability impact analysis state.

justification.description: When the referenced subject is determined to be unaffected, the rationale, reusing the same justification vocabulary as the vulnerability impact analysis. This lets a per-reference negative determination carry its own reason, which the single vulnerability-level analysis justification cannot when different references are unaffected for different reasons. A mitigated but otherwise exploitable condition is expressed here, for example through a protected justification, rather than on `exploitability`.

exploitability.description: The degree to which analysis has substantiated that the vulnerability can be exploited in the referenced subject. This is subject specific and is distinct from `exploitMaturity`, which describes exploitation in the broader threat landscape.

exploitMaturity.description: The maturity of exploitation for the vulnerability in the broader threat landscape, independent of the referenced subject, for example whether a public proof of concept or active exploitation is known.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: The overall confidence of the determination from 0 to 1, where 1 is 100% confidence.

concludedValue.title: Concluded Value
concludedValue.description: The value concluded based on the aggregate of all methods, if available, for example a matched software identifier or a confirmed exploitation primitive.

methods.title: Methods
methods.description: The methods used to extract or analyse the evidence that supports this determination.

tools.title: Tools
tools.description: The tools that produced this evidence, referenced by `refId`.

assertion.description: The party asserting this determination and the perspective from which it is made. Attribution lets determinations from different vantages, such as a supplier and a downstream consumer, coexist and be weighed independently.

timestamp.title: Timestamp
timestamp.description: The date and time at which this determination was made or last held to be valid. Exploitability is time sensitive, so a consumer can use this to judge how current the determination is.

allOf.$comment: A claim that the vulnerability is proven exploitable or has been exploited must be substantiated by at least one demonstrative method of analysis, so that the strongest claims cannot be a bare assertion.

contains.$comment: This is a mixin - this is just a minimal constraint

exploitabilityLevel.title: Exploitability
exploitabilityLevel.description: A graduated indication of how far analysis has substantiated that the vulnerability can be exploited in the affected subject, from mere presence of the component through confirmed exploitation. The value records the strongest level substantiated by the evidence. The levels indicate increasing confidence in exploitability rather than a strictly cumulative sequence, since reachability and precondition satisfiability are related but independent conditions. Mitigation of an otherwise exploitable condition is expressed through the vulnerability impact analysis justification, not through this field.

meta:enum.component-present: The vulnerable component is present, for example established by a software identifier match, without evidence that the vulnerable code is included or reachable.
meta:enum.code-present: The vulnerable code is present in the affected subject, for example the affected function or module is included in the build.
meta:enum.code-reachable: The vulnerable code is reachable in the call graph of the affected subject under some execution path.
meta:enum.runtime-reachable: The vulnerable code has been observed to execute at runtime, for example by runtime instrumentation. This is stronger than static control-flow reachability but does not by itself establish that attacker-controllable input reaches the code.
meta:enum.attacker-reachable: Untrusted or attacker-controllable input can reach the vulnerable code, for example established by data flow or taint analysis.
meta:enum.preconditions-satisfiable: The configuration, environment, or other preconditions required to trigger the vulnerability are satisfiable in the affected subject.
meta:enum.proven-exploitable: Exploitation has been demonstrated in a test or controlled environment, for example by a working proof of concept.
meta:enum.exploited: Exploitation has been observed against the operational subject.

exploitMaturity.title: Exploit Maturity
exploitMaturity.description: The maturity of exploitation for the vulnerability in the broader threat landscape, independent of any particular affected subject. This complements the subject-specific exploitability and aligns with exploit-maturity metrics such as the CVSS Exploit Maturity metric and the SSVC Exploitation decision point. Ecosystem signals such as a CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities listing or an EPSS probability can be carried in `ratings` or `externalReferences`.

meta:enum.not-defined: The exploit maturity is not defined or has not been assessed.
meta:enum.unreported: No exploitation and no public proof of concept are known.
meta:enum.proof-of-concept: A proof of concept is public, or exploitation is currently impractical.
meta:enum.functional: A functional or reliable exploit is available.
meta:enum.active: Exploitation is active or has been observed in the wild.

not.$comment: This schema is hollow: it is not referenced and only remains as a container for structures that are still in use. Itself must not be used for validation.

weaknesses.title: Weaknesses
weaknesses.description: A collection of weaknesses. Each weakness records a source of risk: a flaw, hazard, bias, or other predisposing condition of a subject or its context. Items may be inline weakness objects or references to weaknesses declared elsewhere.

weakness.title: Weakness
weakness.description: A source of risk: a flaw, hazard, bias, or other predisposing condition of a subject or its context that, under certain circumstances, can contribute to a vulnerability, to a threat being realized, or to an adverse or beneficial outcome. A weakness records the condition itself. It may be identified in an external registry, classified by external taxonomies, or named, and at least a name or an identifier shall be provided. What the condition leads to, how likely that is, who or what is affected, and the consequences are not recorded on the weakness. They are expressed by the vulnerability, threat, or risk that references the weakness; for a risk, the consequences are recorded in its impact categories. For example, a bias in data, design, or outputs is recorded as a weakness, and the discrimination or unfair treatment it can cause is recorded in the impact categories of the risk that references it.

refId.description: An optional identifier which can be used to reference the weakness elsewhere using a `refId` or bom-link.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: The kind of source this weakness is. The kind separates a flaw in the subject, an intrinsic hazard, a systematic bias, and a circumstantial predisposing condition, so that weaknesses of one kind can be selected, for example the biases that inform the risks of a machine learning model.

meta:enum.flaw: An imperfection in the design, implementation, manufacture, or configuration of the subject, such as a CWE weakness or a weld imperfection. A flaw is a property of the subject that a vulnerability or threat can exploit.
meta:enum.hazard: An intrinsic property of a material, energy source, or process that can cause harm, such as a toxic substance or a moving part. A hazard exists regardless of any flaw; the risk arises from exposure to it.
meta:enum.bias: A systematic deviation in data, models, measurements, or human judgement that favours some outcomes or groups over others. A bias is a source of risk; its consequences, such as discrimination or unfair treatment, are recorded in the impact categories of the risk that references it.
meta:enum.predisposing-condition: A circumstance of the subject or its context that increases the likelihood or the consequence of an adverse event without itself being a flaw, hazard, or bias, such as a single-source supplier, an obsolete part, or an unsupported dependency.

name.description: The name of the custom kind.

description.description: A description of the custom kind.

name.title: Name
name.description: A short name for the weakness. A name is required when no identifier is given, and is recommended beside an identifier whose registry is not freely readable.

description.title: Description
description.description: A description of the weakness: the condition itself, where it arises in the subject or its context, and the evidence for it. Likelihood, affected parties, and consequences belong to the vulnerability, threat, or risk that references the weakness.

identifiers.title: Identifiers
identifiers.description: Identifiers of this weakness in external registries that assign a stable identifier to each entry, such as a CWE identifier. A weakness may carry identifiers from several registries when they describe the same condition.

categories.title: Categories
categories.description: Classifications of this weakness in taxonomies that name categories without assigning identifiers to entries, such as the NIST SP 1270 categories of bias. Categories complement identifiers; a weakness identified in one registry may also be classified by several taxonomies.

weaknessReference.title: Weakness Reference
weaknessReference.description: A reference to a weakness declared elsewhere, such as in the definitions registry, in another position of the same document, or in another document via BOM-Link. A reference includes the referenced weakness exactly as declared: every position that references the same weakness includes an identical weakness.

ref.title: Reference
ref.description: Reference using bom-link or `refId` to the weakness.

weaknessIdentifier.title: Weakness Identifier
weaknessIdentifier.description: An identifier of a weakness in an external registry, given by the scheme of the registry and the value the registry assigns.

scheme.title: Scheme
scheme.description: The registry that assigns the identifier.

meta:enum.cwe: Identifiers of the [Common Weakness Enumeration](https://cwe.mitre.org/), a community-developed list of software, hardware, and service weakness types.
meta:enum.imdrf-aet: Investigation conclusion codes of Annex D of the [IMDRF Adverse Event Terminology](https://www.imdrf.org/documents/terminologies-categorized-adverse-event-reporting-aer-terms-terminology-and-codes), which classify the root cause of a medical device adverse event.
meta:enum.hfacs: Codes of the [Department of Defense Human Factors Analysis and Classification System](https://navalsafetycommand.navy.mil/portals/100/documents/HF-Enc2-HFACS.pdf), which classify the human and organizational conditions that contribute to mishaps.
meta:enum.sot: Risk category and risk factor identifiers of the [MITRE System of Trust](https://sot.mitre.org/), which classify conditions of suppliers, supplies, and services that affect supply chain risk.
meta:enum.ghs: Hazard statement codes of the [Globally Harmonized System of Classification and Labelling of Chemicals](https://unece.org/about-ghs), which identify the physical, health, and environmental hazards of a substance or mixture.
meta:enum.iso-6520: Reference numbers of [ISO 6520-1](https://www.iso.org/standard/40229.html), which classify geometric imperfections in fusion-welded metallic materials.
meta:enum.iso-iec-24772: Vulnerability codes of [ISO/IEC 24772-1](https://www.iso.org/standard/83629.html), a language-independent catalogue of programming language vulnerabilities.

name.description: The name of the custom scheme.

description.description: A description of the custom scheme.

url.description: URL of the scheme registry or specification.

schemeVersion.title: Scheme Version
schemeVersion.description: The version or edition of the registry that issued the identifier, for example 4.20 for CWE or 8.0 for HFACS.

value.title: Value
value.description: The identifier value as issued by the registry, for example CWE-502.

weaknessCategory.title: Weakness Category
weaknessCategory.description: A classification of a weakness within a taxonomy, given by the taxonomy and the category named or numbered within it.

taxonomy.title: Taxonomy
taxonomy.description: The taxonomy that the category is drawn from.

meta:enum.nist-sp-1270: Categories of bias in artificial intelligence defined by [NIST SP 1270](https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.1270).
meta:enum.iso-iec-tr-24027: Sources of unwanted bias in AI systems and AI-aided decision making defined by [ISO/IEC TR 24027](https://www.iso.org/standard/77607.html).
meta:enum.orx-cause: Cause categories of the [ORX Reference Taxonomy](https://orx.org/operational-risk-reference-taxonomy) for operational and non-financial risk.
meta:enum.hfacs: Causal levels of the [Human Factors Analysis and Classification System](https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/data_research/research/med_humanfacs/oamtechreports/00_07.pdf).
meta:enum.nist-sp-800-30: Types of predisposing condition defined by [NIST SP 800-30 Revision 1](https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.800-30r1).

name.description: The name of the custom taxonomy.

description.description: A description of the custom taxonomy.

url.description: URL of the taxonomy specification.

category.title: Category
category.description: The category within the taxonomy, as named or numbered by the taxonomy.

not.$comment: This schema is hollow: it is not referenced and only remains as a container for structures that are still in use. Itself must not be used for validation.
